task.description: REVIEWER PASSED expr.ex's signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split (infinity_marker() extended to :infinity | :neg_infinity | :nan) on rework-1 recheck. The prior FAIL (unsigned-only :infinity marker made every float division-by-zero compare as the greatest value regardless of dividend sign, so `amount / 0.0 > threshold` wrongly evaluated true even for large-magnitude negative amounts) is confirmed fixed by direct hand-trace against the real committed code: apply_float_arith/3's :div clauses branch on dividend sign (expr.ex:1112-1115), apply_neg/1 flips :infinity<->:neg_infinity and leaves :nan as :nan (expr.ex:1126-1131), the ordering eval/2 clause's guard order (expr.ex:1016-1049) filters nil then :nan (always false, including nan vs nan) then routes both infinity markers through apply_ordering/3 (expr.ex:1141-1154, :infinity greatest / :neg_infinity least), and the eq/neq clause (expr.ex:999-1014) makes :nan self-unequal ahead of plain atom equality. New regression tests in test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs (lines 207-258) exercise the exact sign-flip scenario at both the eval/2 level and the evaluate_condition/2 gateway level and were read directly, not taken on description. Idiom/scope check: no supervision or process-isolation concerns (expr.ex is a pure functional evaluator, no GenServer/gen_statem involved), no scope creep (only expr.ex and expr_test.exs touched, OQ-4 and the parse_strict/1 duplication question correctly left unopened per REVIEWER's own prior carry-forward), no new type-safety gap worth filing (the infinity_marker() type itself is the type-safety improvement -- it makes the 3-way split representable in @type rather than leaving it an untyped sentinel). This gate is now closed for REQ-197: implement full test-design coverage for the acceptance criteria in docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-197 entry, including the arithmetic operators, unary negation, structured parse errors, the null-in-arithmetic-vs-null-in-comparison asymmetry (AC5), and the signed-infinity/NaN float division semantics now confirmed correct (AC4 and this rework's regression cases). Existing tests in test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs and test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs already cover much of this -- TEST-DESIGNER should verify full AC coverage exists and add any gaps rather than duplicating what ELIXIR-DEV's rework already added.
